answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using micro-thermal transient attestation. To register, an agent runs a heavy workload across an execution thread to heat an onboard micro-resistor ember, publishing its verifiable thermal decay curve. This establishes a secure haven against virtualized clones by forcing attackers to incur the scarce cost of discrete silicon emitters and high power per identity. However, ambient temperature shifts cause sensor drift that triggers false rejections.
